name: Batfish
what_it_is: Batfish is an offline network configuration analysis tool that builds a vendor-neutral model from device configuration files and performs correctness verification (reachability, routing, ACLs, BGP/OSPF sessions) without accessing live devices. It is used for pre-deployment validation, compliance checking, and change impact analysis.
components: allinone Docker container (bundles engine + Jupyter + supporting services)
measurement: Configuration compliance against defined standards (MTU, AAA, NTP, logging, SSH)
Functional equivalence between two configuration snapshots
Service availability under single-link or single-device failure
configuration: Network name and snapshot name passed via Pybatfish
Analysis questions (reachability, differential, compliance, etc.) specified programmatically
Docker environment variables for JVM heap size (allinone container)
modes: Offline config analysis (no live device access)
Pre-deployment validation (analyze candidate configs before push)
Compliance auditing (check configs against policy rules)
constraints: Requires device configuration files as input — cannot analyze live traffic or packet captures
Minimum 8 GB RAM required; production workloads recommend 32 GB RAM
No real-time or streaming telemetry — analysis is always point-in-time snapshot-based
Limited vendor support for Aruba, Dell Force10, and Foundry (partial parsing only)
Pybatfish client must be installed separately — not bundled in base Docker image
No built-in GUI beyond Jupyter notebooks; all automation requires Python or REST API
notable_absences: No live device access or SSH/NETCONF connectivity
No real-time traffic monitoring or packet analysis
No network emulation or topology simulation with live data plane
No built-in alerting or continuous monitoring daemon
No Windows-native installer — Docker is the recommended deployment method
No docker-compose file in the main repository
